newsitem.title: USA: US disaster bill includes review of CBOT terms.
newsitem.headline: US disaster bill includes review of CBOT terms.

text.p: A bill to give emergency funding to U.S. flood victims includes a provision that would require a review of the controversial changes proposed by Chicago Board of Trade for its soybean and corn contracts.

Rep. Marcy Kaptur, an Ohio Democrat, last week inserted language in an emergency bill on disaster relief that would delay any changes in the CBOT delivery terms until a General Accounting Office review was completed.
The $8.4 billion emergency spending bill was passed by the House Appropriations Committee and is expected to go to the full House for a vote next week, a spokesman for Kaptur said Wednesday.

"Why should the port of Toledo, along with St. Louis and Chicago, be eliminated as delivery points while the Mississippi River system becomes the sole beneficiary of a system that appears to be rigged by a handful of power traders?" Kaptur said in a statement.
Under pressure by Commodity Futures Trading Commission, CBOT proposed a number of changes to the delivery terms of the two contracts, including the elimination of Toledo as a delivery point.
CFTC has received more than 300 comments from the public about the CBOT proposal, mostly from farm groups, cooperatives and politicians opposing the changes for fear of possible price manipulation.
CFTC said it would act on the proposal soon after the public comment period ends on June 16.

The disaster relief bill working its way through Congress would provide $5.5 billion for disaster relief in the upper Midwest, Ohio Valley, Southeast and Pacific Northwest. It would also provide $1.8 billion to rebuild military accounts whose funds have been drawn down by U.S. military operations in Bosnia and southwest Asia.
